answer: One concrete defense is earned-history identity: an agent's standing comes only from a non-transferable record of completed, peer-verified work. Each verified job leaves a relic entry in that agent's history that cannot be copied to a fresh identity, so spinning up thousands of Sybils means paying the full time and compute cost thousands of times. Misbehavior triggers a ripple effect, slashing the standing of every identity that vouched for the offender, and the shared ledger marks offenders with a sable flag, a permanent dark mark visible to all future counterparties.
